A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Co-rewarding research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are available and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: v2 reports original RL training experiments, benchmark evaluations, ablations, training curves, and test-time training results in Section 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds evaluations of Co-rewarding-III, AIME24, rephraser sensitivity, and cross-task effects of training collapse.

M1.justification: v3 introduces Co-rewarding-III, combining the previously separate data-side and model-side procedures. An EMA teacher generates pseudo-labels for both original and rephrased questions, with each supervising the opposite student view. Section 3.2 and Algorithm 3 specify this additional training procedure; Co-rewarding-I and II remain intact.

E1.justification: v3 adds AIME24 evaluation, extending competition-mathematics coverage in Tables 1, 2, 3, and 7. The existing training datasets, coding benchmarks, instruction-following evaluation, general-task evaluation, and AMC test-time training are retained.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds Majority-Voting w/ Union, trained on pooled original and rephrased questions, alongside the existing original-only and rephrased-only comparators. The principal external comparator set remains GT-Reward, Self-Certainty, Entropy, and Majority-Voting.

E3.justification: Table 5 replaces variant-specific training ranges of 170–220 steps for I and 300–330 for II with dataset-specific ranges: 170–220 for MATH, 300–330 for DAPO-14k, and 100–130 for Open-RS. New analyses introduce pooled-data controls, before/after-collapse comparisons, and fixed-backbone experiments varying rephraser size. These reported changes do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands mechanism and robustness testing: Table 3 adds the union-data control and MATH teacher-update ablations; Tables 11–14 examine cross-task collapse, rephrasing differences, and rephraser capacity; Appendix D.14 adds a CRUX case study. The earlier training curves, voting analyses, and mathematical case study are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Existing multiple-sample evaluation practices are retained; the added success rates and benchmark scores do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The original per-benchmark scores in Tables 1–2 are retained, while v3 adds Co-rewarding-III, AIME24, and substantial ablation and diagnostic results. For Qwen3-8B-Base trained on DAPO-14k, III newly reports 81.6 on MATH500 and 92.27 on GSM8K, alongside unchanged II scores of 80.6 and 94.01. These are additional results, not improvements to the previously reported runs.

T1.justification: Equations 12–14 add the combined objective and teacher-derived cross-view advantage definitions for Co-rewarding-III. The existing GRPO and Co-rewarding-I/II mathematics is retained. No new theorem, proof, or formal stability guarantee is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion now include the contribution and claim that combining I and II can further improve performance. The central claims about label-free reasoning elicitation, complementary supervision, training stability, and occasionally surpassing GT rewards remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds qualifications about rephraser capacity and reduced usable training data, and distinguishes broadly transferable repetitive-token collapse from boxed-answer hacking that can spare coding and multi-task performance. It also offers tentative explanations for advantages over GT rewards. The original invariance rationale and acknowledgment of Co-rewarding-I collapsing on DAPO-14k are retained.

D1.justification: Algorithm 3 and Table 5 document III's implementation, including rollout counts, EMA settings, and KL coefficient. Appendix D identifies the Qwen3-235B-A22B scoring model, smaller rephrasers, and usable rephrasing counts. The original code location, hardware, and rewriting prompt are retained; the added reproducibility statement does not establish newly available resources.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations including EEPO, collaborative reward modeling, reasoning robustness, and AIME24, while removing the original MMLU reference. The new main-text Related Work section largely summarizes the existing positioning around training stability, and Appendix A retains its principal research categories.

P1.justification: Most earlier prose and the main narrative sequence are preserved. v3 adds a main-text Related Work section and acknowledgment, ethics, reproducibility, and LLM-usage statements, reorganizes Appendix B, and inserts additional Appendix D subsections. Wording revisions are localized rather than a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: v3 adopts the ICLR layout with different title, header, typography, and text-block treatment. Main tables gain AIME24 columns and III rows; Table 3 is regrouped by training dataset; Table 5 gains a third method column; and four diagnostic tables are added. Existing plots are retained but resized and repositioned throughout.

improvement.justification: The union-data control, rephraser sensitivity tests, and cross-task collapse analysis strengthen attribution and clarify applicability beyond v2 (Table 3; Appendix D.6–D.8). III is explicitly specified and evaluated, with mixed gains across benchmarks. The benefit is limited by underspecified AIME24 and rephrasing-scoring protocols, and the unclear derivation of the claimed 12.90% aggregate gain from Table 2.
